headline: Cabin Mystery Activity - Collaborative Whodunit for ESL Speaking
outcomes: Students practise question formation, listening, deduction, and role-play inside one memorable mystery
Private role cards create real information gaps, so students need to ask each other for details
The long-form case gives advanced classes a reason to sustain English conversation for most of a lesson
Teachers get an event-style speaking lesson that feels different from a standard discussion prompt
howItWorks: Students receive character roles and case information connected to a mystery on a flight
The class interviews suspects, compares statements, and tracks evidence on the teacher screen
Students decide which clues matter and which stories do not add up
The class submits a final accusation and explains the reasoning before the reveal
teacherUseCases: A special speaking lesson for groups that need sustained conversation and teamwork
Question-formation practice where students must ask follow-up questions for a real purpose
A review or reward lesson that still produces serious language output

faq.q: How many students do I need for Cabin Mystery?
faq.a: Cabin Mystery is designed for at least four students because the activity depends on multiple roles, interviews, and competing pieces of information.

faq.q: Is Cabin Mystery generated for any topic?
faq.a: The current version uses a reviewed static case rather than an open generator. That keeps the mystery coherent and classroom-ready while the format is still being refined.
It works best from B1 upward. Students need enough language to ask follow-up questions, compare details, and explain a theory.

faq.q: Does the teacher have to manage all the clues manually?
faq.a: No. LessonCaptain provides the roles and shared case flow. The teacher facilitates discussion, keeps time, and pushes students to justify claims with evidence.

faq.q: How do students receive their mystery roles?
faq.a: No. Students join through the live browser link and receive their role information without creating an account.
